newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile calls for bids for $172 mln highway project.
newsitem.headline: Chile calls for bids for $172 mln highway project.

text.p: Chile called for international bids Thursday to rebuild a 130-km stretch of highway near the southern city of Puerto Montt and announced it will open bids next week for expansion of Santiago's international airport.
In a statement published in the official gazette, the Public Works Ministry said it was opening bids to rebuild the main highway between Puerto Montt and the town of Rio Bueno in the Tenth Region.

With a budget of 72 billion pesos ($172 million), the highway project includes adding lanes, bridges and exit ramp systems on the full length of the highway, the lifeline for Chile's booming paper and pulp and salmon-raising industries.

Chile has been gradually rebuilding its main north-south motorway known as Route Five through concessions to private public works companies, some of them foreign. Mexican builder Grupo Tribasa SA de CV plans to begin work this month on a nearby sector, the 160-km stretch from Chillan to Collipulli, after winning a $240 million concession.
The builders then have the right to operate and charge tolls on the highway for about 20 years.

The first such concession was granted to Empresa Nacional de Electricidad SA, Endesa public works unit Infrastructura 2000 to build the El Melon highway tunnel north of Santiago in 1995. Since then, the government has used the concession mechanism for nearly all major public works projects in Chile. The goal of President Eduardo Frei's government is eventually to rebuild the entire highway from Puerto Montt as far north as La Serena, about six hours north of Santiago, and build new east-west roads.

The government will call for bids next week for $150 million of expansion work at Santiago's international airport, Aeropuerto Arturo Merino Benitez, said Public Works Deputy Secretary Guillermo Pickering.
"The notices inviting bids will be published this weekend and within a week we will be open to pre-qualifiers," he told reporters.

The expansion calls for improvements at the passenger terminal and a tripling in cargo capacity at the airport on the city's western outskirts by 1999, said Pickering. Technical bids are due to be decided by August 20, he said.
